title: Weight bleed during region decommission caused tier amplification and fallback surge — postmortem
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Summary: On 2025-02-18 during a planned decommission of capacity in eu-west-3, control-plane weight propagation caused a 'weight bleed' where in-flight routing state continued to route traffic to the draining region while per-tier routing weights were widened. This resulted in an amplification of requests to lower-tier model variants and a cascading fallback surge that increased 99th percentile latency and caused a temporary customer-facing error spike for several hosted customers. Impact window lasted ~42 minutes. This postmortem documents detection, root cause, immediate mitigations, and permanent fixes.
timeline: 2025-02-18T10:05:00Z - Scheduled decommission job started for eu-west-3 capacity pool via control-plane orchestrator
2025-02-18T10:07:30Z - Observability alert triggered: tier-3 fallback rate increased by 4x; API 5xx rate rising in hosted-prod region-global metrics
2025-02-18T10:09:15Z - On-call (Ethan) acknowledged and started investigation; linked initial graphs in incident channel
2025-02-18T10:12:00Z - Control-plane reported successful node drain markers for eu-west-3; routing agents continued to receive stale weight vectors for 90s longer than expected
2025-02-18T10:15:00Z - Mitigation: reverted decommission job and triggered immediate circuit-breaker on cross-region routing into eu-west-3; routing weight TTL reduced to 5s
2025-02-18T10:22:00Z - Fallback surge subsided but residual elevated latencies persisted due to KV-cache misses and warmed-down beam search kernels
2025-02-18T10:47:00Z - All metrics returned to baseline; incident declared resolved at 10:50Z after post-checks
detection: Automated SLO alerting detected an unusual increase in fallback invocation and 5xx errors. Noise-robust dashboarding surfaced a correlation between fallback spikes and region decommission signals. Pager on-call alerted within 2 minutes of metric deviation. Centralized routing logs showed weight vectors being applied longer than the expected drain TTL, with widening of per-tier routing weights simultaneously applied by the orchestrator policy.
root_cause: A race between the decommission job that appends a 'drain' tombstone and the control-plane's weight propagation algorithm. The control-plane's batching window for weight delta propagation was extended during the decommission (to reduce churn), which caused an overlap where routes were updated with broadened fallback weights while some routing agents had not yet expired their previous routing entries. This produced an effective temporary widening of tiers and duplicated fallback penalties, increasing traffic funneled to lower-tier variants and producing cache churn in the serving layer.
contributing_factors: Weight propagation batching window increased from 1s to 90s for the decommission run without compensating TTL reductions
Routing agent TTL semantics allowed stale entries to be used while a newer but batched weight slice was applied
Control-plane lacked a strong ordering invariant between drain tombstone application and weight delta commits
KV-cache cold starts on lower-tier variants amplified latency when traffic shifted suddenly
Insufficient canarying of decommission policy changes in dedicated clusters before global execution
immediate_mitigations: We reverted the decommission orchestration policy change, reduced routing weight propagation batching window back to 1s, lowered routing entry TTL to 5s, and activated cross-region routing circuit-breaker to prevent in-flight routing into eu-west-3 while state reconciled. We also warmed KV-caches for tier-2 variants in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 to absorb transient load.
permanent_remediation: Implement strict ordering: apply drain tombstone and confirm agent ACKs before any per-tier weight widening is committed
Add fast-path TTL expiration in routing agents that detects control-plane 'decommission' epoch changes and invalidates stale entries immediately
Limit weight propagation batching during any capacity changes to a max of 5s unless explicitly overridden with a safety flag
Add canary gating for decommission policy changes: execute on a single non-critical cluster and validate metrics for 30 minutes before global rollout
Improve fallback throttling: introduce rate-limiter on fallback invocations per customer to avoid cascading amplification
Telemetry enhancements: emit weight-delta lineage IDs so tracing can correlate which control-plane commit produced a particular routing state

notes: We observed that KV-cache warming reduced p99 by ~120ms in tier-2 variants during the mitigation window
Customer impact was concentrated in customers with aggressive latency SLOs and dynamic route pinning; billing systems were not affected
This incident surfaced a class of bugs where policy optimization (batching/broadening) for operational efficiency conflicts with strict safety ordering
We should treat any future changes to weight propagation as high-risk and gate them behind a change advisory board until these remediations land
